concept: Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines
summary: Source-anchored research for Server selection versus connection and operation deadlines. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The specification makes unset `timeoutMS` preserve existing timeout behavior. An explicit `0` means infinite operation time, but client limits such as `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` still apply. (low confidence)

CSOT is a best-effort maximum. It must cover all blocking sections, but drivers must document exceptions; the specification gives OCSP verification outside driver timeout control as an example that can exceed `timeoutMS`. (low confidence)

Under CSOT, new TCP establishment uses `min(connectTimeoutMS, remaining computedServerSelectionTimeout)`; connection-handshake commands use the remaining `computedServerSelectionTimeout` as their `timeoutMS` value. These minima use the specification’s convention: when 0 means infinite, min(0, other) evaluates to other. (low confidence)

The PyMongo 4.11.2 timeout guide distinguishes `pymongo.errors.ServerSelectionTimeoutError` when no available server is found from `pymongo.errors.NetworkTimeout` when connection establishment or a server response misses the timeout. Its server-side `pymongo.errors.ExecutionTimeout` example warns that an operation may have partially completed. (low confidence)

When checkout requires a new connection under CSOT, TCP establishment uses `min(connectTimeoutMS, remaining computedServerSelectionTimeout)`. Network requests needed to create or authenticate the connection use the lesser of their specified default timeout and the remaining computed selection budget; without a specified default, they use the remaining budget. Handshake commands use the remaining computed selection budget as their `timeoutMS`. These minima use the specification’s convention: when 0 means infinite, min(0, other) evaluates to other. (low confidence)

When `timeoutMS` is set, the CSOT specification requires ignoring deprecated timeout options, including `socketTimeoutMS` and `waitQueueTimeoutMS`; it preserves `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` and `connectTimeoutMS`. (low confidence)

The Node driver documentation defines `connectTimeoutMS` around establishment of a single TCP socket. The CSOT specification retains this limit and also uses it to derive a socket timeout for monitoring connections, which are outside `timeoutMS`. (medium confidence)

The CSOT specification requires drivers to ignore deprecated timeout settings when an operation sets or inherits `timeoutMS`; its deprecated configuration settings include `socketTimeoutMS`, `waitQueueTimeoutMS` and `wTimeoutMS`. (low confidence)

In the PyMongo 4.11.2 guide, `timeout()` bounds all operations inside its block under one deadline, whereas client `timeoutMS` applies to each API call. Nested `timeout()` blocks can shorten the outer deadline but cannot extend it; leaving the block restores the previous deadline. (low confidence)

With `timeoutMS` set, the CSOT specification requires `min(serverSelectionTimeoutMS, remaining timeoutMS)` for selection and checkout. Checkout uses the remaining computed selection budget after selection, rather than receiving a fresh allowance. These minima use the specification’s convention: when 0 means infinite, min(0, other) evaluates to other. (medium confidence)

Under CSOT, after constructing a wire message the driver checks the remaining budget before sending; it sets socket write and then read timeouts from the remaining `timeoutMS`. The response-read timeout covers the aggregate of all reads, rather than restarting for each read. (low confidence)

The Node.js driver documentation distinguishes `connectTimeoutMS` for one TCP connection, `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` for the allowed connection-selection period of `MongoClient.connect`, `socketTimeoutMS` for an already-connected socket, and `maxTimeMS` for execution after an operation reaches the server. The guide permits `maxTimeMS` only on individual operations or cursors. (low confidence)

The CSOT specification defines `timeoutMS` as a best-effort operation budget covering server selection, connection checkout and server-side execution; PyMongo documents the same operation-wide scope. (medium confidence)

The server-selection specification warns that single-threaded blocking topology checks can exceed the selection timeout. CDRIVER-3451 describes a connection attempt whose `connectTimeoutMS` can outlast `serverSelectionTimeoutMS`; this is a documented boundary, not evidence about every released driver. (medium confidence)
Mongoose documents `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` as applying both to initial `mongoose.connect()` attempts and to selecting a server for subsequent operations. (medium confidence)
The CSOT specification excludes commands executed by server-monitoring and RTT-calculation threads from `timeoutMS`. (low confidence)

If `timeoutMS` is unset and `waitQueueTimeoutMS` support remains, the specification preserves separate limits: `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` for selection, `waitQueueTimeoutMS` for checkout, `connectTimeoutMS` for socket establishment, and `socketTimeoutMS` for handshake commands. (low confidence)

The server-selection specification separately warns that single-threaded selection is not a hard deadline: a blocking immediate check can make selection take the configured timeout plus a blocking scan. (low confidence)
